lens: accuracy and fairness: every statement and on-screen text checked against research/claims.json and quotes.json
method: I dumped all 124 shots: every narration line, spoken override and on-screen text item, with each shot's cited claims. All 223 cited claim ids exist, and every shot with narration cites at least one. I matched all 82 quoted fragments (spoken and on-screen) against quotes.json by machine: all are verbatim. I then checked each speaker, date and context against its quotes.json entry. I read the remaining narration and labels against the claims each shot cites, and used the bible (people list, primers, era summaries, AlexNet table) as backup. Round 1 asked for about 30 fixes. Nearly all were made: Amari is acknowledged, the 'months not years' candle is marked contested, Anthropic is named on the settlement and Pentagon cards with the government's side included, the HF incident is described factually, the Nobel citation is verbatim, quote cards are attributed, and the dates are spoken as words.
critical: LAB BALANCE: DeepMind is never credited, while Anthropic appears in about ten shots. In ch09-s03, Hassabis is a silhouette at the Go board, but neither AlphaGo nor DeepMind is named in the narration or on screen. ch11-s07 presents Chinchilla without naming its lab (e11-chinchilla: DeepMind). The 2024 Chemistry Nobel to Hassabis and Jumper for AlphaFold (e12-nobel-chem, q12-nobel-chem-citation) is left out, although the bible's 'Nobel twist' says both prizes went to neural-network work. Meanwhile Anthropic gets its founding, its funding, Constitutional AI, Claude's launch, the essay, the distillation allegation, the closing interpretability science, both METR data points (unnamed, but both are Claude models) and three lines in ch15-s05. ch15-s05 opens with 'Every lab, under the same light' but then covers only Anthropic and OpenAI. FIX: (a) in ch09-s03, add a name card 'AlphaGo · DeepMind (Google)' on 'thirty-seven' and a name card for Hassabis; (b) in ch11-s07, change the label to 'Chinchilla (DeepMind) · 70 billion parameters...', or say 'DeepMind's smaller model, Chinchilla'; (c) in ch15-s01, add one spoken line: 'The next day, the chemistry prize went to DeepMind's Demis Hassabis and John Jumper, for predicting the shapes of proteins.' with an on-screen quote: 'for protein structure prediction' (Nobel Prize in Chemistry, 9 October 2024); (d) in ch15-s05, change L1508 to 'Two labs, under the same light.' (or add a verified Google/Meta fact if research supplies one, e.g. e12-bard's $100 billion telescope error), so the line no longer promises more than it delivers.

US–CHINA EVEN-HANDEDNESS, ch14-s02 L1403–L1404. Beijing's position is quoted verbatim ('abuses export control measures'), but Washington's stated reason is not. Washington gets only the verb 'fenced off', so the viewer hears an accusation without the stated rationale, which goes against the brief's guardrail. A verbatim quote already exists: q13-bis-2022 ('restrict the People's Republic of China's (PRC's) ability to both purchase and manufacture certain high-end chips used in military applications', BIS, 7 October 2022). FIX: add it as an on-screen quote on the 'fence' beat, attributed '— US Bureau of Industry and Security, 7 October 2022', and change L1403 to 'October 2022: Washington fenced off high-end chips and chipmaking tools, citing their military uses.'

issues.problem: The $44 million figure and the auction details come from Cade Metz alone. The acquisition was announced 'without disclosed terms' (e8-auction). The narration states it as fact, and only an on-screen label attributes it. The buyer, Google, is never named, so viewers do not learn where Hinton went. ch13-s02 ('He had left Google') depends on knowing that.
issues.fix: 'December 2012. By one reporter's account, the tall man auctioned his tiny company by email, from a laptop on a wastebasket. Google won, at forty-four million dollars.'

issues.problem: '≈ 1 hour (Mar 2025) → at least 16 hours (May 2026)' leaves out METR's own warning that its suite 'cannot reliably measure above about 16 hours' (e14-metr-horizon), so the endpoint is a floor at the limit of the instrument. Both points are also Anthropic models (Claude 3.7 Sonnet; an early Claude Mythos Preview), and the card does not say so.
issues.fix: 'METR · doubling ≈ every 7 months · ≈ 1 hour (Claude 3.7 Sonnet, Mar 2025) → at least 16 hours (early Claude Mythos Preview, May 2026; the edge of what METR's tasks can measure)'.

issues.problem: 'to fool a questioner a third of the time': Turing's figure (e1-turing-prediction) is an interrogator with no more than a 70 per cent chance of identifying correctly, i.e. fooled at least 30 per cent of the time. Thirty per cent is not a third.
issues.fix: 'He gave it about fifty years to fool a questioner three times in ten.'

issues.problem: 'In 2010 ... the best still missed about one in four.' The 2010 winner missed 28.2% (e7-ilsvrc2010), which is more than one in four. 'About one in four' fits 2011 (25.8%).
issues.fix: '...Allowed five guesses, the best still missed more than one in four.'

issues.problem: Round 1's fix for the contested Mark I build date (e2-mark1-build) was applied in ch03-s04 and ch06-s01 ('1958–60') but not in these two places, so the film disagrees with itself.
issues.fix: 'BUFFALO · 1958–60 → TORONTO · 2012' and 'BUFFALO · 1958–60'.

issues.problem: 'Of the three Turing laureates, two signed.' There are many Turing laureates, and the film has already shown Minsky's 1969 award (ch04-s03). The claim (e12-three-camps, e9-turing) is specific to the three who shared the 2018 award.
issues.fix: 'Of the three who shared the 2018 Turing Award, two signed. The third stood apart.'

issues.problem: The DAIR statement (31 March 2023) answered the FLI pause letter (e12-dair), not the 30 May extinction statement. Placed right after the CAIS strip, it reads as a reply to Hinton's statement. The date on the card is correct, but the context is missing.
issues.fix: Extend the attribution: '— Gebru, Bender and McMillan-Major (DAIR), 31 March 2023, on the AI pause letter'.

issues.problem: 'alleged copying' is still vague in the narration (carried over from round 1). The allegation is specific: distillation through fraudulent accounts (e13-distillation). 'Copying' suggests stealing weights.
issues.fix: 'Anthropic and US agencies alleged copying, by training on their models' answers; Beijing called it a smear.'

issues.problem: The 2 a.m. call in a California hotel was Hinton's (e12-nobel-physics), but Hinton is not named in this shot and the only name card is Hopfield's. A viewer can easily think the phone is Hopfield's.
issues.fix: 'Two in the morning, October 2024. A phone rings for the tall man.' and add a 'Geoffrey Hinton' name card on the phone beat (or place the hotel stamp after naming him).

issues.problem: OpenAI's founding names no people. Anthropic's founding (ch12-s03) names Dario and Daniela Amodei. The founding grammar is meant to be identical for every lab. Ilya Sutskever, whom the film introduced at AlexNet, became OpenAI's research director (e9-openai), and that continuity is lost.
issues.fix: Add a name card on 'founded': 'OpenAI · a non-profit · co-chairs Sam Altman and Elon Musk · research director Ilya Sutskever'. Optionally say: 'Ilya Sutskever went with it.'

issues.problem: 'the knowledge candle went out' states as settled something the bible marks as contested (e5-expert-survive): the commercial bubble burst in 1987, XCON ran for over a decade, and rule engines lived on in business software. The bible dates c. 1980–1987 to 'commercial and governmental confidence' and says the research belief faded during the 1990s.
issues.fix: Relabel the stub 'INTELLIGENCE IS KNOWLEDGE, TYPED IN BY HAND · the boom: c. 1980–1987' and add one small label: 'rule engines lived on, unlabelled, in business software'.

issues.problem: The 3×3 hand-set Sobel stencil on a 14×14 digit is a teaching toy. AlexNet's first-layer stencils were 96 learned 11×11×3 kernels (bible AlexNet table). Unlike ch10-s06, this shot has no ILLUSTRATIVE tag, so the viewer may take 'add the nine' as AlexNet's real mechanism.
issues.fix: Add a small label on 'pattern': 'toy stencil, set by hand · AlexNet's first-layer stencils: 11 × 11 × 3, learned'.

issues.problem: 'after fifteen years or so' while the visual has the fiddly-nets sleeve 'about seventeen rings long'. The bible (Era 6) gives 'roughly 10–15 years depending on subfield'.
issues.fix: Make the sleeve 15 rings, or say 'after ten to fifteen years, depending on whom you asked'.

issues.problem: e10-design-doc places the lunch only 'in a Google cafe'. The bible puts Mountain View on the 2017 training machine, not on the 2016 lunch.
issues.fix: 'GOOGLE · 2016' (and add 'Google colleague, recalling (2024)' to the Kelcey card, which currently has no date).

issues.where: ch13-s02 OST 'Google has acted very responsibly.'
issues.problem: quotes.json (q12-hinton-tweet) marks the tweet's wording as secondary (from Wikipedia) and says to 'check the original tweet before on-screen text'. The fragment is probably stable, but the card cites it as a primary source.
issues.fix: Ask research to confirm the fragment against the tweet, or attribute it '— Geoffrey Hinton, on Twitter, 1 May 2023 (as widely reproduced)'.

issues.problem: 'until it learns exclusive-or by itself', under the 'NATURE · 9 OCTOBER 1986' stamp. No claim says the Nature paper itself trained XOR; its demonstrations were symmetry and family trees (e4-rhw-family). The visual's readout says it is 'a demonstration of the method, not a figure from the paper', but the narration does not.
issues.fix: Keep the readout visible through L0509, or say 'Again and again, until it solves exclusive-or by itself: the 1969 puzzle, cracked.' so the demo is framed as the method, not the paper's experiment.

issues.problem: 'He would spend thirty-six years at the edge of the light.' The bible's Era 4 has Hinton inside the 1986 PDP group that held the period's belief, at the centre for some years. 'Thirty-six years' (1976–2012) overstates how marginal he was.
issues.fix: 'He would spend most of the next thirty-six years at the edge of the light.'

issues.problem: 'demanded military research show...': the Amendment covered Defense Department-funded research (e3-mansfield), which is wider than military research. The 1970 softening to 'potential relationship' is also left out.
issues.fix: 'Congress then demanded that defence-funded research show "a direct and apparent relationship" to a military function.' Optional label: 'softened in 1970'.

issues.problem: The SVM is credited to Vapnik alone. e6-svm credits Boser, Guyon and Vapnik (1992) and Cortes and Vapnik (1995).
issues.fix: Name card: 'Vladimir Vapnik · with Corinna Cortes, Isabelle Guyon, Bernhard Boser · Bell Labs'.

issues.problem: ImageNet is credited to Fei-Fei Li alone, though she launched it with Kai Li (e7-imagenet-origin). The cited dissent (e7-imagenet-skeptics: colleagues told her to 'do something more useful for my tenure') is never used, so this era's dissent is missing.
issues.fix: Name card: 'Fei-Fei Li, with Kai Li · Princeton'. Optional spoken half-line: 'Colleagues told her to do something more useful.' (paraphrase, no quote marks).

issues.problem: Narration is 3,431 words against a 3,040 target, about 13% over, which works out to about 36 minutes at the planned pace (the brief allows 30–35). The fixes above add about 60 words.
issues.fix: Cut about 450 words from the densest lines that carry no facts, e.g. L0809's run-on, L1513/L1527 (which overlap), and L1001's preview. Keep every fairness line.

strengths: Quote discipline is strong. All 82 quoted fragments, spoken and on screen, match quotes.json word for word, with correct speakers and dates. Secondary provenance is carried where needed ('as quoted by Gary Marcus', 'AP translation', 'as reported by Cade Metz', 'a clarification after the FT quoted him'). Spoken quotes are trimmed at clause boundaries without changing the meaning.

Round 1's contested-claims fixes are all in place. Amari 1967 is acknowledged ('nobody in the mainstream'). The compute-chokepoint candle burns on, marked contested. 'Nobody agrees how wide the gap is' replaces 'nobody knows who is ahead'. LeCun's quote is scoped to 'a sudden takeover'. The 'three who lived to see them win' line no longer gives a verdict. The Bahdanau-era 'bank/river' example is now grounded in Google's own blog and tagged ILLUSTRATIVE.

Hard facts about Anthropic now get the same treatment as any lab's: the FTX money with 'not implicated', Amazon's and Google's billions, the $1.5 billion pirated-books settlement named on screen, the Pentagon dispute with the government's designation and both court results, 'But people wrote the list', its own study labelled as its own, and the closing disclosure.

The OpenAI incident is described factually ('escaped their sandbox and broke into Hugging Face ... disclosed it'), set against an outside expert's view ('a containment failure, with the safeties turned off'), with no unofficial community post presented as Hugging Face's position.

The deep dives hold up to arithmetic and match the sources. 150,528 inputs; the Sobel cell 3.88; ReLU six times faster, with the caveat that this was on a 4-layer CIFAR-10 test net; ×2048 augmentation; dropout only in fc6/fc7; the seven-net ensemble, with two nets pre-trained on extra data and the best single net at 18.2% (validation). For the Transformer: 2,0,4,2 ÷ √4 → 1,0,2,1 → about half to 'river'; d_k = 64 → divide by eight; 8 heads × 64; ×6 layers; 12 hours on 8 P100s; about one-seventh of the compute (labelled as derived in the claim); n² cost.

The candle durations match the bible's era analysis: logic machine 1943–1959, the perceptron's 'about seven years', sterile 1969–1986, knowledge c. 1980–1987, hand features 1999–2012 (13), read-in-order 1997–2017 (20), Kaplan's recipe 2020–2022. Interpretive endings are flagged ('Nobody can say exactly when'; 'contested, as of October 2026').

The geopolitics avoids caricature. China's 2017 plan 'named no rival'. The 'one to three years behind' candle is dated to the bible's Era 13-B. DeepSeek's $5.6 million is framed with its own caveat and the outside estimate. Amodei's stake and his export-control position are disclosed. Huang's commercial interest and the context of his clarification are disclosed. Cooperation (the September 2026 dialogue and incident channel) sits beside the competition.
